appearances.sentence: He abandoned his family.
appearances.solution: The correct answer is (a) supported, as it is the opposite of “abandoned,” meaning to leave or desert. “Supported” means to provide help or assistance, which contrasts with abandoning. The other options (encouraged, pleased, saved) do not serve as direct opposites.

appearances.sentence: ABATE
appearances.solution: To abate is to become less intense or less widespread, as when a storm or a fever abates. Increase and maintain both go the wrong way, and provoke means to stir something up rather than to reduce it. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: The oppressive pollution was noticed to have abated after the unseasonal rainfall.
appearances.solution: 'Abated' means reduced in intensity; 'mitigated' is the nearest synonym meaning lessened. Common error: choosing 'suppressed' which implies forceful stopping. Matches option A: mitigated.

appearances.sentence: They are making plans for the abatement of the nuisance within a specified time.
appearances.solution: 'Abatement' means a reduction or decrease. Its antonym is 'accumulation' (an increase or build-up). Matches option C: accumulation.

appearances.sentence: To abolish poverty would be to destroy the soil upon which mankind produces the virtues conducive to higher civilization
appearances.solution: The word 'abolish' means to formally put an end to something; 'eradicate' is the closest synonym meaning to completely destroy. Matches option B: eradicate.

appearances.sentence: Macbeth is an abominable figure.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. "Abominable" means hateful/detestable; its opposite is "attractive" (pleasing, admirable). "Abhorrent" and "repugnant" are synonyms. "Reputable" means respectable but is not the direct opposite of abominable; "attractive" is the cleaner antonym of abominable (loathsome vs. pleasing).

appearances.sentence: The horror and abomination of the system of Sati in India was condemned thoroughly.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Abomination' means intense disgust/loathing. The opposite is 'adoration' (intense love/admiration). 'Abhorrence' and 'detestation' are synonyms; 'termination' is unrelated.

appearances.sentence: He nodded absently throughout the meeting.
appearances.solution: The antonym task requires identifying the word opposite in meaning to 'absently' (inattentively/distractedly). 'Alertly' means in an attentive, watchful manner — directly opposite. Matches option B: alertly.

appearances.sentence: The abstruse style of the speaker left the students disinterested and fidgety.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. Abstruse means difficult to understand, obscure — recondite is a direct synonym (obscure/abstruse).

appearances.sentence: His conversations are always absurd.
appearances.solution: The key concept is antonym identification. 'Absurd' means wildly unreasonable; its antonym is 'rational' (sensible, logical). Matches option D: rational.

appearances.sentence: The decision was absurd for many of the members of the team.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Absurd' means ridiculous, illogical, senseless. Its opposite is 'reasonable' (sensible, logical). 'bizarre' and 'meaningless' are synonyms; 'thoughtful' is less precise as an antonym than 'reasonable'. 'reasonable'.

appearances.sentence: What the critic said about this new book was ABSURD?
appearances.solution: “ABSURD” means something that is illogical, unreasonable, or ridiculous. The opposite of this would be “sensible,” which refers to some- thing that is logical, reasonable, or makes sense. The other options—”interesting,” “impartial,” and “ridic- ulous”—do not directly contrast with “absurd” as clearly as “sensible” does.

appearances.sentence: Abundant food was available for the soldiers in the mess.
appearances.solution: Abundant means existing in large quantities; plentiful is the closest synonym. Matches option B: plentiful.

appearances.sentence: ACCOST
appearances.solution: To accost someone is to go up to them and speak to them, often boldly or uninvited, so address is the match. Hesitate describes the opposite behaviour, and injurious and selective are not verbs of approach at all. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: He was accused by the entire community after he failed in the mission.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Accused = charged/blamed; opposite = vindicated (cleared of blame). Incriminated/indicted/arraigned are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: The exemptions granted to State institutions for acquiring informed consent from processing personal data in many cases appear to be too blanket.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Acquiring' means obtaining/getting. 'Obtain' is the nearest synonym.

appearances.sentence: It could not have been expected that, with such a bent of mind of the people, there should have been much activity for the cultivation of the physical sciences in this part of the world.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. The underlined word is the noun 'activity', so its antonym must also be a noun. 'Indolence' (laziness, habitual inactivity) is the only noun among the options; 'dull', 'dormant' and 'idle' are adjectives and are near-synonyms of one another, which is the standard three-lookalike-distractors pattern. 'Dull' is the opposite of 'bright' or 'lively', not of 'activity'.

appearances.sentence: Businessmen who lack acumen cannot be expected to be very successful.
appearances.solution: 'Acumen' means the ability to make good judgements; 'sharpness' (keenness/shrewdness) is the closest synonym. 'Fairness' and 'righteousness' relate to ethics, not mental agility. Matches option B: sharpness.

appearances.sentence: They will not admit children under fourteen.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. "Admit" here means to allow to enter / let in; the nearest synonym is "receive" (to receive/allow in). "Accept" and "concede" relate to admitting a fact, not admitting a person; "receive" matches admitting children into a place.

appearances.sentence: Children adore the cricket players.
appearances.solution: The word "adore" means to like or love someone or something deeply. Its opposite would be "condemn," which means to express strong disapproval. Therefore, "condemn" is the antonym of "adore" in this sentence.

appearances.sentence: I think they would wish for some more adornment around the school campus for the special function.
appearances.solution: 'Adornment' means adding decorative elements; the direct synonym is 'decoration'. Matches option B: decoration.

appearances.sentence: The CEO has been praised for his adroit management of the company's financial recovery.
appearances.solution: Adroit means skilful and deft in handling a matter. Skillful and dexterous simply restate it, and ambidextrous names a related manual facility rather than its reverse. Gauche means clumsy and tactless, and the pair is exact even in origin, since adroit comes from the French for right-handed and gauche from the French for left-handed. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: ADROIT
appearances.solution: The antonym of “adroit” is (b) Clumsy. “Adroit” means skillful or proficient, particularly in handling situations or tasks. The opposite of skillful is “clumsy,” which means awkward or lacking in skill.

appearances.sentence: Choose the word nearest in meaning to: ADULATION
appearances.solution: 'Adulation' is excessive admiration or praise, i.e. 'flattery'. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: Advocacy is one major component of any new programme.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Advocacy = active support for or promotion of a cause. Nearest synonym is promotion.

appearances.sentence: Unlike his brother, he is affable.
appearances.solution: 'Affable' means friendly and easy to talk to; the antonym is 'reserved' (not openly friendly). 'Irritable' is close but 'reserved' is the more precise opposite. Matches option A: reserved.

appearances.sentence: Choose the word which is most OPPOSITE in meaning to the word given: AFFLUENT
appearances.solution: Affluent means wealthy, so its opposite is poor. 'Fluent' is a sound-alike trap. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: I attempted to aggrandize the CEO’s high status in the company to sweet talk him into signing off on the deal.
appearances.solution: To aggrandize someone is to build up their power, wealth or importance, that is to elevate their standing. Abase means to lower or humiliate and is the opposite. Perigee, the point of nearest approach, is offered as a false pair for apogee, and an aeon is a vast stretch of time. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: The leader said, "I am aghast with the developments so far. I will take time to understand this."
appearances.solution: 'Aghast' means struck with shock and horror, so 'horrified' is nearest in meaning. 'Sad' is far too mild for a word that carries dismay, and the speaker's follow-up - that he will need time to understand this - fits shock rather than satisfaction or amusement. Matches option D.

appearances.sentence: The leader said, "I am aghast with the developments so far. I will take time to understand this."
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Aghast' means shocked or horrified; 'horrified' is the nearest synonym.

appearances.sentence: This is akin to a contractual relationship that places obligations on the entities entrusted with data.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Akin to' means similar to/related to. 'Similar' is the nearest synonym.

appearances.sentence: He was fully alive to the need for making adjustments.
appearances.solution: 'Alive to' means conscious/aware of something. He was fully aware of the need for adjustments. Matches option C: aware of.

appearances.sentence: The members of the group expressed their allegiance to their leader
appearances.solution: Allegiance = loyalty/commitment; nearest synonym is commitment. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: His ALLEGIANCE to the party was suspect from the very beginning.
appearances.solution: “ALLEGIANCE” refers to loyalty or commitment to a group, cause, or individual. In this context, it suggests the person’s loyalty to the party was in question from the start. The other options, such as “servility,” “obedience,” and “passivity,” do not fully capture the idea of loyalty, which is the most fitting meaning for “allegiance.”

appearances.sentence: The 'Jataka Tales' present moral narratives in the form of allegories.
appearances.solution: 'Allegories' are extended symbolic narratives; the nearest synonym is 'parables', which are short symbolic stories conveying moral lessons. Options A and B are short sayings, not narrative forms. Matches option D: parables.

appearances.sentence: ALLURE
appearances.solution: The antonym of “allure” is (d) Repel. “Allure” means to attract or tempt someone, while “repel” means to drive someone away or cause them to feel disinterested or disgusted, which is the opposite.

appearances.sentence: Choose the word which is most OPPOSITE in meaning to the word given: ALTERCATION
appearances.solution: An altercation is a noisy quarrel or dispute; a compromise is the settling of a dispute, hence its opposite. 'Challenge' and 'opposition' are closer to synonyms. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: Often, the context and structure of an ambiguous statement is difficult to discern.
appearances.solution: 'Ambiguous' means open to multiple interpretations; 'cryptic' (mysterious/unclear) is the closest synonym. 'Explicit' is an antonym. Matches option C: cryptic.

appearances.sentence: The partners maintained an amicable relation­ ship after selling the business.
appearances.solution: Amicable means friendly and good-natured. Amiable, gracious and mellow all repeat that sense in different registers. Surly means bad-tempered and unfriendly, which is the reverse of an amicable relationship. Matches option D.

appearances.sentence: Choose the word which is most OPPOSITE in meaning to the word given: ANIMOSITY
appearances.solution: Animosity is strong hostility or ill will, so its opposite is affection or love. 'Lust', 'luck' and 'loss' are unrelated. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: The portal will help victims and complainants to anonymously report cyber crime.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Anonymously' (without revealing identity) is nearest to 'incognito'. Directly/unfailingly/in situ do not mean anonymous.

appearances.sentence: He is always anxious.
appearances.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Anxious' means worried or nervous; 'worried' is the closest synonym. Matches option A: worried.

appearances.sentence: There are plenty of graduates anxious for work.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Anxious for work' = eagerly/keenly wanting work. 'Eager' is the nearest synonym. 'Composed' and 'indifferent' are near-opposites; 'prominent' is unrelated.

appearances.sentence: I would beg of all friends not to rush to Birla house nor try to dissuade me or be anxious about me.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. "Anxious" means worried/full of care and concern; its opposite is "careless" (free from care/anxiety, unconcerned). "Certain" is the opposite of anxious only in the sense of doubt, but "careless" (carefree, without anxiety) is the standard antonym of anxious here.

appearances.sentence: She faced the situation with aplomb.
appearances.solution: Aplomb means self-assurance and steadiness under pressure, that is, composure. Grace refers to elegance of movement rather than calm confidence, fear is the opposite, and arrogance is excessive self-importance. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: The pole vaulter reached the apogee of height in the competition, catapulting him into first place.
appearances.solution: The apogee is the highest point reached, and apex names that same summit. Heyday is a peak in time, a period of greatest success, whereas the sentence is measuring height in a vault and not a stretch of years. Inane means silly and accommodate is a verb. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: The archaic thinking leads to unfounded beliefs.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. Archaic = very old, outdated. Antonym is modern. (Antiquated, outmoded, beyond the times are synonyms.)

appearances.sentence: It was indeed arduous to cross streets in New York.
appearances.solution: 'Arduous' means demanding/difficult; its direct antonym is 'effortless' (requiring no effort). 'Pleasant' is related but not the strongest antonym. Matches option B: effortless.

appearances.sentence: Arvind had an arduous task to attend to.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Arduous' means difficult and laborious; its opposite is 'easy and effortless'.

appearances.sentence: Arrogance is a hallmark of his nature.
appearances.solution: Arrogance means exaggerated sense of self-importance; 'conceit' is the nearest synonym. Matches option C: conceit.

appearances.sentence: In the modern times, we find that most social relationships are rather artificial.
appearances.solution: Artificial here means put on or insincere, so the word required is one meaning real and unaffected, which is genuine. Decent, excellent and adorable are all terms of approval, but approval is not the opposite of falseness. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: In the modern times, we find most social relationships are rather artificial.
appearances.solution: The word "artificial" refers to something that is not natural, often meaning to something fake. The opposite of this would be "genuine," which means real, authentic, or sincere. Therefore, "genuine" is the antonym of "artificial" in the context of social relationships.

appearances.sentence: Geomorphologists ascertain several wonderful facts about our earth.
appearances.solution: 'Ascertain' means to find out or discover with certainty, which is closest to 'verify'. Matches option A: verify.

appearances.sentence: The cause of the accident is yet to be ascertained, but police officials suspect the driver of the vehicle allegedly fell asleep.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Ascertained' means found out for certain or determined; 'determined' is nearest.

appearances.sentence: The cause of the accident is yet to be ascertained, but police officials suspect the driver of the vehicle allegedly fell asleep.
appearances.solution: To ascertain something is to find it out for certain, so 'determined' is nearest in meaning. 'Curtained' is only a sound-alike, 'thought of' suggests conjecture rather than establishing a fact, and 'being known' will not fit the pattern 'is yet to be ___'. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: Living hidden away in the mountains suited his ascetic character.
appearances.solution: 'Ascetic' means severely self-disciplined and abstinent — austere. Matches option D.

appearances.sentence: Language is an instrument for asserting one's identity, attitude and perspective.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Asserting' means declaring/affirming positively. Its opposite is 'denying' (refusing to affirm). 'declaring', 'supporting' and 'propagating' are synonyms/associates. 'denying'.

appearances.sentence: There was a combination of agrarian colonising tendencies with the assertion of local landlord power that was able to assimilate pioneer peasants.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Assertion' means a confident, forceful statement/affirmation. The opposite is 'denial'. 'Insistence', 'averment', and 'statement' are synonyms of assertion.

appearances.sentence: For Gandhiji, India's religious and linguistic diversity was an asset, not a liability.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Asset' (a valuable thing, contrasted with liability) is nearest to 'advantage'. Attribute is a quality (close but not the contrast intended); advantage best fits the 'asset vs liability' opposition.

appearances.sentence: The public watched in astonishment as he took a sudden jump from the bridge.
appearances.solution: 'Astonishment' means great surprise or amazement. 'Wonderment' is the closest synonym. Matches option C: wonderment.

appearances.sentence: The atheist wrote a novel disproving the existence of a higher power.
appearances.solution: An 'atheist' is one who disbelieves in the existence of God — a disbeliever. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: In India, it has become easy to attack cultural artefacts these days.
appearances.solution: Attack in the context of cultural artefacts means to assail or damage; assault is the closest synonym. Matches option B: assault.

appearances.sentence: Why does fire attract insects?
appearances.solution: Attract means to draw towards; the antonym is repel (to push away). Matches option C: repel.

appearances.sentence: He found her extremely attractive and charming.
appearances.solution: Attractive means pleasing or appealing; its antonym is 'repulsive' meaning causing disgust. Matches option C: repulsive.

appearances.sentence: Many communication problems can be attributed directly to misunderstandings and inaccuracies.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Attributed to' means ascribed to/credited to a cause. 'Ascribed' is the exact synonym.

appearances.sentence: The student's striking audaciousness disturbed long-standing social hierarchies on campus.
appearances.solution: 'Audaciousness' means bold daring; its antonym is 'timidness' (lack of courage). Options A and B are synonyms. Matches option C: timidness.

appearances.sentence: He had the audacity to blame him.
appearances.solution: 'Audacity' means a willingness to take bold risks; rude boldness. Its antonym is 'politeness'. Matches option D: politeness.

appearances.sentence: The birth of his child decidedly proved to be an auspicious event in his life.
appearances.solution: 'Auspicious' means favourable/lucky; its antonym is 'ominous' (threatening/inauspicious). 'Useless' is too general, 'precious' and 'unforgettable' are not opposites. Matches option B: ominous.

appearances.sentence: He was born on a very auspicious day.
appearances.solution: The word 'auspicious' means giving a sign of future success (favourable); its antonym is 'ominous' — giving a sign of future misfortune. Matches option C: ominous.

appearances.sentence: This piece of art is authentic.
appearances.solution: 'Authentic' means genuine; its antonym is 'fake'. Matches option D: fake.

appearances.sentence: His aversion is known to all.
appearances.solution: 'Aversion' means a strong dislike or opposition; 'hostility' is closest in meaning among the options. Matches option B: hostility.

appearances.sentence: The king's son was banished due to the political rivalry.
appearances.solution: The concept is synonym identification: 'banished' means expelled/sent away from a place. 'Deported' is nearest in meaning — both involve forced removal from a territory. Matches option A: deported.

appearances.sentence: Barring a decision of such disputes, other matters relating to the election of President or Vice-President may be regulated by law made by Parliament.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Barring = except for, excluding, leaving out. Antonym is including. (Excepting, without, excluding are synonyms.)

appearances.sentence: Choose the word nearest in meaning to: BEAUTIFUL
appearances.solution: 'Handsome' means good-looking/beautiful and is the keyed synonym. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: Beauty lies in the eyes of the beholder.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Antonym of 'Beauty' (loveliness, charm) is 'Inelegance' (lack of grace/beauty). 'Allure' and 'Charm' are synonyms; 'Ideal' is unrelated.

appearances.sentence: His behaviour was quite belligerent.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Belligerent' means hostile, aggressive, eager to fight. Its antonym is 'amiable' (friendly). Bellicose, antagonistic and combative are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: She is a benevolent individual.
appearances.solution: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and kind; its antonym is 'malevolent' (having evil intentions). Matches option C: malevolent.

appearances.sentence: BENIGN
appearances.solution: The correct answer is (b) Hostile because “benign” refers to something gentle, kind or harmless, often used to describe something that causes no harm, such as a benign illness or behaviour. The opposite of this would be “hostile”, which refers to being unfriendly, aggressive or harmful. Thus, “hostile” is the most appropriate antonym.

appearances.sentence: The highest award was bestowed upon her for her yeoman service.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Bestowed' means given or conferred; its opposite is 'withdrawn' (taken back). Conferred/imparted are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: The highest award was bestowed upon her for her yeoman service.
appearances.solution: To bestow an award is to give or confer it, so the opposite is to take it back: 'withdrawn'. 'Conferred' is placed first as a straight synonym to catch a hurried reader; 'imparted' also means to give, and 'imbibed' means to absorb. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: They describe the act as a blatant betrayal of faith.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Betrayal' means treachery/disloyalty. 'Treachery' is the nearest synonym; the others are antonyms.

appearances.sentence: He is biased against the students from cities.
appearances.solution: 'Biased' means unfairly prejudiced; its antonym is 'impartial' (treating all equally). Matches option D: impartial.

appearances.sentence: In the winters, the countryside view is bleak and the house is drafty.
appearances.solution: 'Bleak' means lacking vegetation, or cold and miserable. Its antonym is 'verdant' (green with vegetation, lush). Matches option B: verdant.

appearances.sentence: Blend the grains to make a smooth paste.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Blend' = mix/combine. The opposite is 'separate'. 'Mingle', 'coalesce', 'amalgamate' are synonyms of blend.

appearances.sentence: There was much to boast about the quality of his work.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Boast = praise/extol oneself; opposite = deprecate (express disapproval/belittle). Bluster/brag/flaunt are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: His arguments are not valid. People consider it bombastic.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Bombastic' means high-sounding, pompous and inflated in language. Its opposite is 'straight forward' (plain, direct). 'verbose' is a near-synonym; 'outdated' and 'not true' are unrelated. 'straight forward'.

appearances.sentence: The harder we kick, the better the ball bounces back.
appearances.solution: The synonym of 'bounces back' (springs back on impact) is 'recoils' (springs back). Matches option A: recoils.

appearances.sentence: The sky is boundless.
appearances.solution: Boundless means having no limits; its antonym is 'finite' meaning limited. Matches option D: finite.

appearances.sentence: His bounty is limitless.
appearances.solution: 'Bounty' means generosity or liberality in giving; 'benevolence' (goodwill and generosity) is the nearest synonym. Matches option A: benevolence.

appearances.sentence: None but the brave deserves the fair.
appearances.solution: 'Brave' means courageous; its antonym is 'coward' (someone lacking courage). Matches option B: coward.

appearances.sentence: Brevity is the soul of wit.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Brevity' = shortness, conciseness. The opposite is 'verbosity' (wordiness). 'Concision', 'economy', 'terseness' are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: His speeches were models of brevity.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Brevity' means shortness, conciseness. The nearest synonym is 'concision'. 'Lengthiness' is the antonym.

appearances.sentence: The Managing Director of the company declared that he is broke and there is a need to seek support from the government.
appearances.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Broke' in informal usage means having no money; 'bankrupt' is the closest formal synonym. Matches option A: bankrupt.

appearances.sentence: BUCOLIC
appearances.solution: Bucolic means of the countryside, pastoral, so rustic is the synonym. The other three point the other way - urban, metropolitan and citified are all city words, clustered together to tempt a guess made from the sound of the word rather than its sense. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: Mr. Kumar works as a bursar in the sports academy.
appearances.solution: A bursar is a person who manages the financial affairs of an institution; the closest synonym is 'accountant'. Matches option B: accountant.

appearances.sentence: The flood situation during the monsoon this year was calamitous.
appearances.solution: 'Calamitous' means involving a calamity; catastrophic; the nearest synonym is 'catastrophic'. Matches option B: catastrophic.

appearances.sentence: Mr. Khanna is quite CALLOUS towards the victims of earthquake.
appearances.solution: “Callous” means showing an insensitive or cruel disregard for others. The opposite of this is “sympathetic,” which means showing compassion or care for others’ suffering. The other options do not directly contrast with “callous.”

appearances.sentence: Since the callow baker was new to cake deco­ rating, she did not know how to properly frost the multi-layer cake.
appearances.solution: Callow describes someone not yet matured by experience, and the standard dictionary gloss of the word is simply immature. The sentence supplies the evidence by saying the baker was new to cake decorating. Puerile and childish both mean silly in the manner of a child, which is a judgement on behaviour rather than on inexperience, and seasoned means experienced and is the opposite. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: His candid remarks impressed the authorities.
appearances.solution: The word "candid" means honest, open and straightforward. The opposite of "candid" in this context is "guarded," which refers to being reserved in expression, often to avoid revealing too much.

appearances.sentence: CANDID
appearances.solution: Candid describes speech that is open and truthful even when the truth is unwelcome, so a candid opinion is a frank one. Deceptive is its direct opposite, while careless and dull describe manner or quality rather than honesty. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: His candid opinions have won him many friends.
appearances.solution: 'Candid' means outspoken and honest; its synonym is 'frank'. 'Kind', 'courteous', and 'generous' relate to manner, not openness. Matches option D: frank.

appearances.sentence: The village headman was old and cantankerous.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Cantankerous' means bad-tempered, argumentative, quarrelsome. The nearest synonym among the options is 'ill-tempered'. 'Polite' is an antonym; 'weak' and 'serious' are unrelated.

appearances.sentence: He is always captious.
appearances.solution: 'Captious' means tending to find fault or raise petty objections. Among the options, 'faultfinding' is the closest synonym. Matches option C: faultfinding.

appearances.sentence: Choose the word that is synonymous with "CAPTIVATE".
appearances.solution: To captivate is to hold someone's attention so completely that they are charmed by it, and 'enchant' carries that same sense of delighted attention. Discouraging, boring and repelling a person all push them away, which is the opposite of what captivating does, so all three are antonyms rather than synonyms. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: CARDINAL
appearances.solution: The most appropriate synonym for “cardinal” is (a) Essential. “Cardinal” refers to something of primary importance, fundamental, or essential. Therefore, it aligns with the meaning of “essential.”

appearances.sentence: We carried on the search for the missing person.
appearances.solution: 'Carried on' means continued. Its antonym is called off (cancelled/stopped). Matches option D: called off.

appearances.sentence: We worship celestial beings.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Celestial (heavenly) is opposite to earthly/terrestrial.

appearances.sentence: Choose the word nearest in meaning to: CENSURE
appearances.solution: 'Censure' means to express strong or formal disapproval, i.e. to criticize severely. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: Women gather in the community park on a regular basis to chant prayers for the benefit of all.
appearances.solution: 'Chant' means to say or sing repeatedly; 'recite' is the nearest synonym in the context of prayers. Matches option D: recite.

appearances.sentence: The house was full of chaos when I reached.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. Chaos is opposite to order. Disorder/confusion are synonyms; uniformity is sameness, not the direct opposite of disorder.

appearances.sentence: All business activities need not result in profit-making. There is a need to be charitable.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Charitable' means generous and kind/benevolent; its opposite is 'malevolent' (ill-willed). 'Gracious'/'lenient' align with charitable.

appearances.sentence: All business activities need not result in profitmaking. There is a need to be charitable.
appearances.solution: 'Charitable' means generous and kindly disposed towards others, so the opposite is 'malevolent', which means ill-disposed and wishing harm. 'Gracious' and 'lenient' lie on the same side as the underlined word, and 'unforeseen' has nothing to do with temperament. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: The princess charming was the centre of attraction today.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. "Charming" (attractive, pleasing) is opposed by "repulsive" (causing disgust/aversion). "Enchanting", "hypnotic" and "fascinating" are synonyms of charming.

appearances.sentence: CHASTE
appearances.solution: The antonym of “chaste” is (c) Lustful. “Chaste” refers to being pure, especially in terms of sexual behaviour, or abstaining from indulgence in lustful desires. The opposite of “chaste” would be “lustful,” which refers to strong, often uncontrolled and desires.

appearances.sentence: The crowd CHEERED the cricketer.
appearances.solution: “Cheered” means to express joy, approval, or encouragement, especially in response to someone’s performance. In this case, the crowd showing support for the cricketer fits with the meaning of “encouraged.”

appearances.sentence: I cherish your company.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Cherish means to value/hold dear; deprecate (disapprove/belittle) is the opposite.

appearances.sentence: The teacher chided the pupil.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Chided means scolded; commended (praised) is the opposite. The other three are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: He was rather childish.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Childish (immature) is opposite to seasoned (mature/experienced). Infantile is a synonym.

appearances.sentence: The possibility of success was chimerical.
appearances.solution: 'Chimerical' means fanciful, imaginary or impossible; its opposite is feasible. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: The power of the monarchy was circumscribed by the new law.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Circumscribed' = restricted/limited. 'Constrained' (restricted, confined) is the nearest synonym. 'Circumvented' (evaded) is a confusable trap by sound but means to get around, not to limit.

appearances.sentence: The group held some clandestine meetings to resolve the matter.
appearances.solution: 'Clandestine' means kept secret or done secretively. Its antonym is 'public'. Matches option D: public.

appearances.sentence: His clandestine affairs were suspicious.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Clandestine (secret, hidden) is opposite to conspicuous (open, obvious). Covert/furtive are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: The sky is clear today.
appearances.solution: Clear in the context of sky means transparent and unclouded; its antonym is 'opaque' meaning not transparent. Matches option B: opaque.

appearances.sentence: A new show is trying to change the cliched depictions of women in animation.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Cliched' means overused or unoriginal; 'hackneyed' is the nearest synonym.

appearances.sentence: Choose the word which is most OPPOSITE in meaning to the word given: COAX
appearances.solution: To coax is to persuade someone gently to do something; to dissuade is to persuade them not to. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: Whether the rewards are in commensurate with the efforts or not, a society will always have workaholics and the shirk work groups.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Commensurate' means proportionate/equal in measure; its opposite is 'disproportionate'.

appearances.sentence: The Colonel ordered the Soldiers to meet him in the commissary.
appearances.solution: A commissary is a store or canteen, especially in a military context. Matches option D: canteen.

appearances.sentence: Having got excited she opened up the Pandora's Box which led to lot of commotion.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Commotion' means noisy disturbance/uproar; 'uproar' is nearest in meaning.

appearances.sentence: Amid commotion the leader and his supporters remained passive.
appearances.solution: 'Commotion' means a state of confused and noisy disturbance. Its antonym is 'quietude' (a state of stillness and calm). Matches option A: quietude.

appearances.sentence: What we lack in the current times is compassion.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Compassion' means sympathetic concern for others; its opposite is 'indifference'. 'Empathy' is a synonym.

appearances.sentence: What we lack in the current times is compassion.
appearances.solution: The item asks for the word opposite in meaning to the underlined one. 'Empathy' is a near synonym of compassion, and 'carefulness' and 'hardship' are unrelated to it. 'Indifference' is the absence of the fellow feeling that compassion names. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: Each child develops his/her competency based on the contexts and the inputs for learning.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Competency' means ability/capability to do something; 'capability' is nearest in meaning.

appearances.sentence: Raj is a competent carpenter.
appearances.solution: 'Competent' means having the necessary ability. Its synonym is 'capable'. Matches option A: capable.

appearances.sentence: His success in the preliminary examination made him COMPLACENT.
appearances.solution: “COMPLACENT” refers to being self-satisfied, often to the point of being unaware of potential dangers or the need for further effort. The opposite of this is “discontented,” which means feeling dissatisfied or lacking satisfaction, driving one to strive for improvement. The other options do not represent the opposite meaning of “complacent”.

appearances.sentence: We must not become complacent about the progress of the technology.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Complacent' means self-satisfied, smugly content. The nearest synonym is 'contented'. 'Discontented' is the antonym.

appearances.sentence: The complexity of the issue baffled everyone.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Complexity = intricacy. Complacency is a distractor by sound only.

appearances.sentence: The COMPLEXITY of the issue baffled everyone. Choose the word most similar in meaning to COMPLEXITY.
appearances.solution: 'Complexity' means 'intricacy'; complacency is a similar-sounding distractor with an unrelated meaning. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: After a good meal, it is important to pay a compliment to the chef.
appearances.solution: 'Compliment' means an expression of admiration or praise. Its synonym is 'praise'. Matches option B: praise.

appearances.sentence: COMPUNCTION
appearances.solution: Compunction is the prick of conscience felt over a wrong done - guilt or remorse - and repentance carries exactly that sense of regret. The word has nothing to do with equipment, excitement or confusion. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: CONCEDE
appearances.solution: The antonym of “concede” is (b) Reject. “Concede” means to admit or acknowledge something, often reluctantly, while “reject” means to refuse or deny something, which is the opposite.

appearances.sentence: He was quite concerned about his son's career.
appearances.solution: 'Concerned' means worried/interested. Its antonym is indifferent (having no particular interest). Matches option B: indifferent.

appearances.sentence: The party was excellent, and I would like to thank all the people concerned.
appearances.solution: Concerned means interested or involved; the antonym is uninvolved. Matches option D: uninvolved.

appearances.sentence: Scientists are concerned whether the oceans and land biosphere will take up as much carbon in the future as they presently do.
appearances.solution: The antonym of 'concerned' (worried, troubled) is 'indifferent' (having no particular interest or concern). Matches option B: indifferent.

appearances.sentence: CONCILIATION
appearances.solution: Conciliation is the act of reconciling or making peace; the opposite is confrontation (hostile opposition). Matches option D.

appearances.sentence: There are four concurrent handloom fairs around the city.
appearances.solution: 'Concurrent' means happening at the same time; its antonym is 'consecutive' (following in sequence). Matches option A: consecutive.

appearances.sentence: The first step in precipitation is condensation.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Condensation' is vapour turning to liquid; its opposite process is 'evaporation' (liquid turning to vapour). The other options are not opposites in this physical sense.

appearances.sentence: The guilty appealed to the jury to condone his punishment.
appearances.solution: The word "condone" means to forgive or overlook an offense or wrongdoing. The opposite of "condone" is "condemn," which means to express strong disapproval of something or to declare it wrong. Therefore, "condemn" is the antonym of "condone" in this context.

appearances.sentence: Don't condone such acts which lead to unrest in the country.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. Condone means to overlook / pardon / disregard an offence. 'Overlook' is nearest; 'punish' is the opposite.

appearances.sentence: He is one of the confidants of the leader and can influence the decision of the government.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. A confidant is a trusted intimate/close friend to whom secrets are confided, so (b) 'intimate' and (c) 'close friend' are synonyms. The section asks for the OPPOSITE, and (a) 'opponents' is the antonym; (d) 'colleague' is merely a neutral associate, not an opposite. KEY FIX PENDING: the stored key D was derived when option (a) had been overwritten with (b)'s text, so the antonym was invisible; it must move D -> A via scripts/cds/apply-key-fixes.ts.

appearances.sentence: His confidence is high.
appearances.solution: 'Confidence' means self-assurance; its antonym is 'diffidence' (lack of self-confidence). Matches option A: diffidence.

appearances.sentence: They are confident of success.
appearances.solution: 'Confident' means feeling certain about one's abilities. Its antonym is diffident (modest/lacking self-confidence). Matches option C: diffident.

appearances.sentence: Among its distinctive features is a conflation between land, a national(ised) language, and a people.
appearances.solution: The block asks for the opposite of the underlined word. Conflation names the running together of two separate things into one. Amalgamation and meld both name that same merging, and an emulsion is likewise two substances held together as a single mixture, so all three sit on the same side as the underlined word. By contrast, a constituent is one component of a whole, an element kept distinct rather than fused, so it alone points the other way. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: CONNOTE
appearances.solution: The term “Connote” means to suggest or imply something in addition to the primary meaning. It refers to the ideas or feelings that a word invokes beyond its literal definition. “Convey” also means to communicate or express something, which fits the meaning of “connote.” The other options, like “comment,” “criticize,” and “care,” do not capture the meaning of “connote.”

appearances.sentence: The project wasted a considerable amount of time and money.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Considerable' = large, significant. The opposite is 'trifling' (small, insignificant). 'Substantial', 'plentiful', 'abundant' are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: Choose the word nearest in meaning to: CONSIGNEE
appearances.solution: A 'consignee' is the named person to whom goods are sent; among the options 'nominee' (a designated/named person) is closest. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: He was conspicuous because of his colourful shirt.
appearances.solution: Conspicuous means → clear ≠ Unnoticeable

appearances.sentence: The advertisements were all posted in a conspicuous place.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Conspicuous means clearly visible, attracting attention — nearest meaning is noticeable.

appearances.sentence: There are many factors that constrain the philosophy of job enrichment in practice.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Constrain' means restrict/limit/hold back. Its antonym is 'Support' (to enable/help forward). 'Restrict' is a synonym; 'Oblige'/'Pressure' do not reverse it.

appearances.sentence: Her smile was contagious.
appearances.solution: Contagious means spreading from person to person; 'catching' is the closest synonym meaning 'infectious'. Matches option D: catching.

appearances.sentence: He is such a leader that his actions are contagious.
appearances.solution: The item asks for the word nearest in meaning to the underlined one. Something contagious spreads from one person to another, which is what 'transmittable' means: the leader's conduct catches on among those around him. 'Effective' is the tempting distractor because it also describes influence, but it says nothing about spreading. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: He is such a leader that his actions are contagious.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Contagious' means spreading from one to another; 'transmittable' is the nearest synonym.

appearances.sentence: Choose the word nearest in meaning to: CONTEMPLATION
appearances.solution: 'Contemplation' is deep, reflective thought, i.e. 'meditation'. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: CONTEMPT
appearances.solution: Contempt is the feeling that a person or a thing is worthless and beneath serious consideration. Measure each of the four words against that sense. Praise, respect and approval all express a favourable estimate of something, so each of them stands opposed to contempt rather than close to it, and because three separate words share that same opposed relation, no one of them could be singled out over the other two. Scorn is different. It means precisely the open disdain that contempt describes, and the two words are used interchangeably in ordinary writing, as in treating a suggestion with contempt or with scorn. It is the only word in the list that is near in meaning to the given word rather than opposite to it. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: To him everything I did was considered contemptuous.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Contemptuous' means scornful/disdainful; its opposite is 'reverential' (showing deep respect).

appearances.sentence: Only three candidates are now in contention for the title.
appearances.solution: 'In contention' means having a possibility of winning or achieving. 'Chance of winning' best captures this meaning. Matches option C: chance of winning.

appearances.sentence: Twenty first century has turned out to be a century of problems contrary to the thinking that it would be a better time.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Contrary to' means opposite to / in conflict with. Its opposite is 'similar' (in line with, agreeing). 'different' and 'divergent' are synonyms of contrary; 'good faith' is unrelated. 'similar'.

appearances.sentence: Please use conversational language.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. Conversational means informal, everyday speech.

appearances.sentence: I had some deepest convictions reflected in my work.
appearances.solution: 'Convictions' means firmly held beliefs or principles. 'Firm beliefs' is the closest match. Matches option B: firm beliefs.

appearances.sentence: He first convulsed and then collapsed on the floor.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. To 'convulse' is to shake violently / suffer involuntary spasms. The nearest synonym is 'shivered'. The collapse context supports a physical shaking sense rather than crouching, shouting, or crying.

appearances.sentence: Sachin is very cooperative by nature.
appearances.solution: 'Cooperative' means willing to help. Its closest synonym is 'complaisant' (eager to please). Matches option A: complaisant.

appearances.sentence: The witness corroborated word for word the statement of the victim.
appearances.solution: 'Corroborated' means confirmed/supported; its antonym is 'denied'. 'Accepted' and 'confirmed' are synonyms, 'repeated' is unrelated. Matches option C: denied.

appearances.sentence: These exercises will counteract the effects of stress and tension.
appearances.solution: The concept is antonym identification: 'counteract' means to oppose/neutralize. 'Exacerbate' means to make worse, which is the opposite of neutralizing. Options B, C, D are synonyms of counteract. Matches option A: exacerbate.

appearances.sentence: Bad tendencies are to be countered by good ones until all that is evil disappears.
appearances.solution: 'Countered' means to oppose or neutralise; 'opposed' is the closest synonym. 'Balanced' implies equilibrium, not active resistance. Matches option A: opposed.

appearances.sentence: He gave me a counterfeit coin.
appearances.solution: 'Counterfeit' means made in imitation of something genuine; fake. Matches option B: fake.

appearances.sentence: Human craving for comfort leads to anxiety.
appearances.solution: Antonym means opposite in meaning; 'craving' means a strong desire or longing. The opposite of craving (desire) is 'complacency' (self-satisfaction, absence of desire). Matches option D: complacency.

appearances.sentence: Some of the criticisms which they had to put up were very unfair.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. "Criticism" (finding fault, disapproval) is opposed by "appreciation" (favourable judgement, praise). "Scold", "scorn" and "censure" are synonyms of criticism.

appearances.sentence: She is a rather crooked woman.
appearances.solution: Crooked means dishonest or devious; its antonym is 'straightforward' meaning honest and direct. Matches option C: straightforward.

appearances.sentence: This decision is crucial for me.
appearances.solution: The synonym of 'crucial' (of great importance at a decisive moment) is 'momentous' (of great importance). Matches option A: momentous.

appearances.sentence: He is essentially a crude person.
appearances.solution: 'Crude' means rough or unrefined. Its antonym is 'refined'. Matches option B: refined.

appearances.sentence: The crux of the issue was that there was no evidence to prove the accused guilty of the act.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Crux' means the central/most important point; 'core' is nearest in meaning.

appearances.sentence: The river Ganges culminates in the Bay of Bengal.
appearances.solution: 'Culminates' means reaches a climax or final point. Its antonym in this context is 'originates' (where a river begins). Matches option C: originates.

appearances.sentence: Cultural diversity in the working place is good for business.
appearances.solution: Cultural diversity means variety of different cultures; the antonym is uniformity (sameness). Matches option A: uniformity.

appearances.sentence: He was too cunning for her.
appearances.solution: 'Cunning' implies slyness and craftiness; 'dodgy' (evasive, untrustworthy) is the nearest synonym in this context. Matches option D: dodgy.

appearances.sentence: He is suffering from a curable disease.
appearances.solution: The antonym of 'curable' (able to be treated) is 'terminal' — leading inevitably to death, incurable. Matches option C: terminal.

appearances.sentence: The gradual CURTAIL in the expenditures made them tensed.
appearances.solution: The term “Curtail” means to reduce or diminish something. Its opposite is “increase,” which means to grow or expand.

appearances.sentence: Standing before a judge in a courtroom can be daunting for anyone.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Daunting' means intimidating/discouraging. Its antonym is 'Encouraging'. 'Demoralizing', 'Off-putting' and 'Uncomfortable' are closer to synonyms.

appearances.sentence: DAUNTLESS
appearances.solution: The term dauntless means showing courage, fearlessness, and determination in the face of challenges. It describes someone who is not easily intimidated and is resolute in their actions. Therefore, fearless and determined is the most accurate meaning.

appearances.sentence: He gave a dazzling performance at the opera.
appearances.solution: The concept is synonym identification: 'dazzling' means impressively brilliant. 'Brilliant' is the nearest synonym. Matches option A: brilliant.

appearances.sentence: Now we can have another dazzling thought, as an outcome of my brilliant research!
appearances.solution: 'Dazzling' means extremely bright or impressive. Its antonym is 'murky' (dark, gloomy). Matches option B: murky.

appearances.sentence: The biggest debate among scientists today is about cloud feedback.
appearances.solution: The antonym of 'debate' (a formal discussion with opposing viewpoints) is 'agreement' (consensus, accord). Matches option D: agreement.

appearances.sentence: Her left leg was paralysed due to a debilitating disease.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Debilitating' means making someone weak or infirm; the nearest in meaning is 'crippling'.

appearances.sentence: Justice prevailed and the murderer was decapitated.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Decapitated' means to cut off the head. The nearest synonym is 'beheaded'.

appearances.sentence: Early medieval period was not a combination of urban and rural civilization. It was not a period of urban decay as claimed by some.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Decay' means decline or deterioration; its opposite is 'survival' (growth/flourishing). The other options are near-synonyms of decay.

appearances.sentence: Early medieval period was not a combination of urban and rural civilization. It was not a period of urban decay as claimed by some.
appearances.solution: The item asks for the word opposite in meaning to the underlined one. 'Waste away', 'decomposition' and 'spoil' are all synonyms of decay, so none of them can be the answer. 'Survival' is the only word that runs against the sense of a town falling into ruin. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: Relatives of deceased have been informed about the accident.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Deceased' means dead. Its direct opposite is 'alive'. 'dead' is a synonym; 'injured' and 'survived' are related but not true antonyms. 'alive'.

appearances.sentence: To be able to decipher something is wonderful.
appearances.solution: 'Decipher' means to convert coded or unclear information into an understandable form; 'decode' is the direct synonym. Matches option A: decode.

appearances.sentence: His dedication is known to all.
appearances.solution: 'Dedication' means commitment and zeal; its antonym is 'apathy' (lack of interest or enthusiasm). Matches option C: apathy.

appearances.sentence: I have a fascination for deep waters.
appearances.solution: Deep means extending far down; its antonym is 'shallow' meaning not deep. Matches option D: shallow.

appearances.sentence: They successfully defused the situation.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. To 'defuse' a situation is to reduce its tension/danger. The nearest synonym is 'mitigated' (lessened). 'Activated' is the opposite; 'mediated'/'narrated' do not match the meaning.

appearances.sentence: He is a loving father and takes great delight in his children.
appearances.solution: 'Delight' means great pleasure. Its antonym is disgust (strong disapproval/revulsion). Matches option D: disgust.

appearances.sentence: A glance at a beautiful object gives us delight.
appearances.solution: The word 'delight' means great pleasure or happiness; 'happiness' is the closest synonym among the options. Matches option B: happiness.

appearances.sentence: The judge told that he would analyze the evidence and then deliver the verdict.
appearances.solution: Deliver the verdict means to pronounce or announce it formally; pronounce is the closest synonym. Matches option D: pronounce.

appearances.sentence: The deluge affected the population.
appearances.solution: 'Deluge' means a heavy flood or downpour; its antonym is 'drought' (absence of rain). Matches option B: drought.

appearances.sentence: She is considered to be demure by her family members.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Demure' means modest/reserved; its opposite is 'brazen' (bold/shameless).

appearances.sentence: It is the general reaction of some people to denounce any new proposal by enthusiastic professionals.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. To 'denounce' is to condemn/criticise publicly. The opposite is 'appreciate' (value, commend). 'Criticise' and 'censure' are synonyms; 'comment' is neutral.

appearances.sentence: DENSE
appearances.solution: Dense means thickly packed; the opposite is sparse (thinly distributed). Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: Mohan was living in a deplorable condition.
appearances.solution: The concept is antonym identification: 'deplorable' means wretched/shameful. Options A, B, C all carry negative connotations similar to deplorable; 'commendable' means praiseworthy, which is the direct opposite. Matches option D: commendable.

appearances.sentence: Friends have always DEPLORED my unsociable nature.
appearances.solution: “DEPLORED” means to express strong disapproval or to feel regret about something. In this context, it suggests that the friends have always felt regretful or disapproved of their unsociable nature. The other options do not fit the meaning of “deplored” in this context.

appearances.sentence: His derisive behaviour has led to the situation we now face.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. Derisive means expressing contempt/ridicule. As an adjective describing 'behaviour', 'contemptuous' is the nearest matching adjective; 'mockery' is a noun and doesn't fit the adjective slot.

appearances.sentence: The employees rejected the derisory pay offer.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Derisory' (of an amount/offer) means ridiculously small, insultingly inadequate. In the pay-offer context the nearest synonym is 'inadequate'. 'Derogatory' relates to disrespectful remarks, not a pittance amount.

appearances.sentence: I was awe-inspired by his designation.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Designation refers to an official title or position/rank.

appearances.sentence: The manner in which this exercise has been undertaken leaves much to be desired.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Desired' means wished for/wanted. 'Wish for' is the nearest synonym.

appearances.sentence: He felt desolated after he lost his business.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Desolated means feeling abandoned, forlorn and bleakly deserted; 'deserted' is the nearest in meaning. 'Annoyed' is too mild and 'joyful'/'strong' are opposites.

appearances.sentence: In my state of despair, I confessed everything.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. Despair = hopelessness; opposite = elation (great joy). Despondency is a synonym.

appearances.sentence: Hitler was a despot.
appearances.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Despot' means a ruler with absolute power; 'dictator' is the closest synonym. Matches option B: dictator.

appearances.sentence: The police detained me today amidst busy traffic.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Detained = held/confined; opposite = released. Impeded/confined/held are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: It was felt that the decision to remove the group from the exercise would be detrimental to the organization.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Detrimental means harmful/damaging; 'disadvantageous' is nearest. 'Beneficial' is the opposite.

appearances.sentence: The institution decided to give Mrs. Roy's job to her son not because she was a social worker, but because she had died in harness.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Die in harness' means to die while still actively employed, i.e. before retirement.

appearances.sentence: Our differences are growing day by day.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Differences (in the sense of disputes between people) = disagreements. Discrepancies means inconsistencies between things, not interpersonal differences.

appearances.sentence: Our DIFFERENCES are growing day by day. Choose the word most similar in meaning to DIFFERENCES.
appearances.solution: In the sense of interpersonal conflict, 'differences' means 'disagreements'; 'discrepancies' denotes inconsistencies, not disputes. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: Police had to resort to tear gas to diffuse tension among the crowd.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Diffuse = to spread out/disperse over a wide area. Antonym is concentrate. (Scatter, disperse, strew are synonyms of diffuse.)

appearances.sentence: DILAPIDATED
appearances.solution: Dilapidated describes a building that has fallen into disrepair through age and neglect, which is what ruined means. Decorated and repaired describe the opposite condition, and expanded is about size rather than state of repair. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: Choose the word nearest in meaning to: DILIGENT
appearances.solution: 'Diligent' means hard-working and careful, i.e. 'industrious'. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: The employ only DILIGENT workers.
appearances.solution: “DILIGENT” refers to someone hardworking, careful, and persistent in their work. The opposite of diligent would be someone lazy, not putting in effort or avoiding work. The other options, such as “unskilled,” “careless,” and “idle,” do not directly capture the opposite meaning of “diligent” as clearly as “lazy.”

appearances.sentence: He is diligent in submitting assignments.
appearances.solution: 'Diligent' means careful and hardworking. Its closest synonym is 'conscientious'. Matches option D: conscientious.

appearances.sentence: The hotel room had dingy walls.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Dingy' means gloomy, dull, and dirty. The nearest in meaning is 'dark and dirty'.

appearances.sentence: He discontinued the work due to pressure.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Discontinued (stopped) is opposite to resumed (started again).

appearances.sentence: The members have taken a unanimous decision to discord some of the rulings of the Managing Committee on problems relating to maintenance.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Discord' means disagreement/conflict. Its antonym is 'Accord' (agreement, harmony). 'Dissension', 'Dispute', 'Friction' are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: She has always been disdainful of people who haven't been to college.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Disdainful' = showing contempt/scorn. The opposite is 'respectful'. 'Contemptuous', 'dismissive', 'scornful' are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: The whole audience showed a disdainful attitude during the match.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Disdainful' means scornful/contemptuous. Its antonym is 'Respectful'. (Sneering and Mocking are synonyms.)

appearances.sentence: There is a feeling of disenchantment among the members of the group.
appearances.solution: 'Disenchantment' means a feeling of disappointment after discovering something is not as good as believed. Matches option B: disappointment.

appearances.sentence: The official accused of espionage was found to be disingenuous.
appearances.solution: 'Disingenuous' means not candid or sincere; its antonym is 'scrupulous' (honest and careful). Options B, C, D are synonyms of disingenuous. Matches option A: scrupulous.

appearances.sentence: The doctor dismembered the patient's finger first and then cured the ailment.
appearances.solution: 'Dismembered' means to cut apart or divide; in medical context the closest option is 'dissected' (to cut apart for examination/surgery). Matches option B: dissected.

appearances.sentence: He disowned his royal legacy and became a commoner.
appearances.solution: The concept is synonym identification: 'disowned' means to refuse to acknowledge or renounce. 'Abandoned' is the nearest in meaning among options. Matches option B: abandoned.

appearances.sentence: Though he was arrogant, I could not dispense with his services.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Dispense with his services' means to do without / end them; 'terminate' is nearest in meaning.

appearances.sentence: He has been part of the all dissident activities.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Dissident = in opposition to official/established policy; rebellious. Synonym is rebellious. (Conformist and supportive are opposites.)

appearances.sentence: The politician was a dissident.
appearances.solution: The key concept is antonym identification. 'Dissident' means a person who opposes official policy; its antonym is 'conformist'. Matches option C: conformist.

appearances.sentence: His relatives dissuaded him from giving up the job.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Dissuade = to advise/persuade someone NOT to do something. Antonym is persuaded. (Discouraged, advised against, deter are synonyms.)

appearances.sentence: This painting has a distinctive element which can be noticed well.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Distinctive' means distinguishing/unique/special. Its antonym is 'Common'.

appearances.sentence: Every habitat has some distinctive vegetation which defines the eco-system.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Distinctive' means characteristic, distinguishing, special/unique. Its opposite is 'common' (ordinary, shared, not distinguishing). 'unique' and 'special' are synonyms; 'unfamiliar' is unrelated. 'common'.

appearances.sentence: They were distraught on receiving the news.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Distraught' means deeply agitated/upset; its opposite is 'composed' (calm).

appearances.sentence: She got the divorce within no time.
appearances.solution: The synonym for 'divorce' in legal context is 'annulment' (formal dissolution of a marriage). Matches option C: annulment.

appearances.sentence: The dodgy behaviour of the leader led to her fall
appearances.solution: Dodgy = suspicious; nearest synonym among options is dubious. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: Amit is a dogmatic person.
appearances.solution: 'Dogmatic' means inclined to lay down principles as absolute truths; its antonym is 'amenable' (open to suggestion, willing to agree). Matches option B: amenable.

appearances.sentence: They were fed-up with his doltish behaviour.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Doltish' means stupid, foolish (a dolt is a stupid person). The nearest synonym is 'imbecilic' (foolish/stupid). 'Wise', 'clever' and 'precocious' are antonyms or unrelated.

appearances.sentence: Some animals live a dormant life.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. Dormant (inactive/sleeping) is opposite to active. Latent/inert/sluggish are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: DOUGHTY
appearances.solution: The term doughty means brave, courageous or valiant. It describes someone who is resolute and determined, especially in the face of danger or adversity. The word valiant is the closest synonym, as it also refers to someone showing courage or bravery.

appearances.sentence: We must adopt drastic measures to control population growth.
appearances.solution: 'Drastic' means extreme and severe in effect. The nearest synonym among options is severe. Matches option D: severe.

appearances.sentence: He drowned in the flood water last year.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Drowned = died/went under water. 'Submerged' (went under water) is nearest in meaning. Swam/floated are opposite; swarmed is unrelated.

appearances.sentence: He DROWNED in the flood water last year. Choose the word most similar in meaning to DROWNED.
appearances.solution: 'Drowned' (sank and died under water) is closest to 'submerged'. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: Autumn is rather a dry season.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Dry = arid. Humid/moist/rainy are opposites.

appearances.sentence: Autumn is rather a DRY season. Choose the word most similar in meaning to DRY.
appearances.solution: 'Dry' is synonymous with 'arid'; humid, rainy and moist are opposites. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: Ramesh is a very dubious character.
appearances.solution: The word 'dubious' means hesitating or doubting; its antonym is 'trustworthy' — certain and reliable. Matches option C: trustworthy.

appearances.sentence: Her dynamic nature impressed everyone.
appearances.solution: Dynamic means characterized by constant change and progress; 'evolutionary' is nearest in meaning as it implies development and change. Matches option C: evolutionary.

appearances.sentence: We caught him eavesdropping outside the window.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Eavesdropping' = secretly listening to others' private conversation. 'Listening secretly' is the exact synonym.

appearances.sentence: Her ideas have always been eccentric.
appearances.solution: 'Eccentric' means unconventional or odd; its antonym is 'normal'. Option B (strange) is a synonym. Matches option C: normal.

appearances.sentence: He delivered an eccentric speech.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Eccentric = unconventional/odd; opposite = normal. Odd/peculiar/idiosyncratic are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: In those days many monarchs enjoyed vast ecclesiastical powers.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Ecclesiastical' means relating to the church/spiritual matters; its opposite is 'temporal' (worldly/secular).

appearances.sentence: The poems of Kabir are ecstatic in nature.
appearances.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Ecstatic' means feeling intense happiness or elation; 'rapturous' means expressing great enthusiasm or delight. Matches option C: rapturous.

appearances.sentence: I fully believe that the cornerstone of good policy is an electorate that is educated on the national issues.
appearances.solution: The antonym of 'educated' (knowledgeable/informed) is 'ignorant' (lacking knowledge). 'Cerebral' and 'erudite' are near-synonyms; 'enlightened' is also similar. Matches option C: ignorant.

appearances.sentence: Everything about him, especially his talkative nature, proclaims his effeminacy.
appearances.solution: Effeminacy is the display of qualities conventionally regarded as womanly in a man, so its direct antonym is manliness. Boorishness means rudeness, aggressiveness means hostility and attractiveness means appeal, none of which is the paired opposite. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: Efficacy of the project needs an examination.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Efficacy' means effectiveness/ability to produce a desired result. Its antonym is 'Inefficiency'. (Efficiency and Effectiveness are synonyms.)

appearances.sentence: She was effusive in her praise.
appearances.key: expressing approval while exhibiting strong feelings
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Effusive means expressing feelings in an unrestrained, gushing way — expressing approval while exhibiting strong feelings.

appearances.sentence: He was effusive in his praise.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Effusive' means expressing feelings in an unrestrained, gushing manner. Its antonym is 'reticent' (reserved, restrained). Exuberant, profuse and voluble are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: One feels elated when someone praises one's work.
appearances.solution: 'Elated' means filled with high spirits, so its opposite is the low-spirits word, 'depressed'. 'Excited' and 'feels good' sit on the same side as the underlined word, and 'sober' means serious or restrained rather than downcast, which makes it a much weaker contrast. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: One feels elated when someone praises one's work.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Elated' means very happy or joyful; its opposite is 'depressed'. Feels good/excited are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: The policemen kept questioning the criminal but failed to ELICIT the truth.
appearances.solution: In this context, “ELICIT” means to draw out or obtain information, such as the truth, through questioning. “Evoke” could be used for emotions or responses, “wrest” means to forcibly pull something, and “extort” involves obtaining something through threats or force, which doesn’t fit in the context of the question.

appearances.sentence: ELOQUENT
appearances.solution: Eloquent describes speech or writing that is fluent, forceful and persuasive, so expressive is the closest match. Silent and awkward are its opposites in fluency, and rigid describes inflexibility rather than the power to express. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: He speaks eloquently and can pull crowds.
appearances.solution: The item asks for the word opposite in meaning to the underlined one. To speak eloquently is to speak clearly, fluently and persuasively, so 'expressively', 'powerfully' and 'fluently' all restate it. 'Confusingly' is the only word that denies the clarity eloquence implies. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: He speaks eloquently and can pull crowds.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Eloquently' means fluently and persuasively; its opposite is 'confusingly'. The other options are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: Wars leave behind a large number of emaciated soldiers in the camps of both the victorious and the vanquished.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Emaciated' means abnormally thin/wasted; its opposite is 'hefty' (large and heavy).

appearances.sentence: Emboldened by his success, the leader now plans to go ahead with the plan and implementation.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. To embolden = to give courage/confidence to. 'Emboldened by his success' means encouraged by it. Nearest synonym is Encouraged.

appearances.sentence: He was enamoured of his own golden voice.
appearances.solution: To be enamoured of something is to be filled with liking or admiration for it. The sentence says he was enamoured of his own golden voice, that is, he admired and delighted in it. Being very fond of something carries exactly that sense of liking and admiration. Being concerned with something means only being involved with it; being obsessed with something names a much stronger, unhealthy fixation than the word carries; and being imbued with something means being filled with a quality, not with affection for it. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: Some people complain when they encounter a small misfortune in the course of their thoroughly happy life.
appearances.solution: The word 'encounter' means to come across or meet unexpectedly; among the options, 'run into' (to meet by chance) is the closest synonym. Matches option A: run into.

appearances.sentence: Words of endearment always touch me.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Endearment expresses affection/fondness.

appearances.sentence: The leader's endurance paid and he won the elections.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Endurance is the capacity to persist/withstand — nearest to patience.

appearances.sentence: The hot sun ENERVATED the labourer to the extent that he collapsed.
appearances.solution: “Enervated” means to make someone feel drained of energy or strength, which is similar in meaning to “weaken,” as it implies a reduction in strength or vitality. The other options are not synonyms: “alleviate” means to reduce or ease something (typically pain), “energise” means to give energy or vitality, and “elevate” means to raise or lift something, neither of which fits the context of feeling weakened.

appearances.sentence: Any classroom should provide an engaging environment for learners.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Engaging means attractive/interesting/holding attention; 'appealing' is the nearest in meaning.

appearances.sentence: He was ENGROSSED in writing a story.
appearances.solution: “ENGROSSED” means to be fully absorbed or deeply involved in something, usually to the point of losing awareness of other things. So, in this context, it means the person was deeply focused or absorbed in writing a story. The other options like “absolved,” “interested,” and “engaged” are related but do not capture the full intensity of being “engrossed.”

appearances.sentence: He succumbed to ennui and despair.
appearances.solution: 'Ennui' is a feeling of listless boredom; its opposite is excitement. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: He tried to enshroud the fact that they were already married.
appearances.solution: To enshroud is to cover up or conceal, so its opposite is to reveal, that is, to uncover what was hidden. State, declare and announce all mean to say something openly but none of them carries the specific sense of exposing something concealed. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: The teacher asked her students to understand the ensuing problems and address them suitably.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Ensuing = following, coming afterward, subsequent. Antonym is retrospective (looking back / relating to the past). (Subsequent and consequent are synonyms; en suite is unrelated.)

appearances.sentence: Social media trends are ephemeral.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Ephemeral' means short-lived; its opposite is 'everlasting' (the others are synonyms of ephemeral).

appearances.sentence: She accepted the prospect of her medical treatment with equanimity.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Equanimity means calmness and composure. The opposite is agitation; tranquillity, composure and placidity are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: The leader's views were equivocal on the contentious issue.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Equivocal' means open to more than one interpretation, ambiguous, unclear. Its antonym is 'clear'. Options obscure, ambiguous and vague are synonyms, not antonyms.

appearances.sentence: Choose the word which is most OPPOSITE in meaning to the word given: ERUDITE
appearances.solution: Erudite means having or showing great learning, so 'unscholarly' is the opposite. 'Educated' and 'scholarly' are synonyms and act as traps. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: The writer's erudition in science is revealed in every page of the book.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Erudition' means deep learning/knowledge; its opposite is 'ignorance' (a noun, matching the noun erudition).

appearances.sentence: ESCULENT
appearances.solution: Esculent means fit to be eaten, so edible is a direct synonym. The word is unrelated to legality, to discontent or to disguise. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: It was EVIDENT from his gestures that he was feeling guilty.
appearances.solution: The word “evident” means clear. The antonym “hidden” means concealed or not apparent, which is the opposite of evident.

appearances.sentence: The officer in charge of the operations has been expelled for the excesses.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. The underlined word IS 'expelled' (option A repeats it). Among the options, the nearest synonym to 'expelled' (driven out, dismissed) is 'Expelled' itself; the test intends the closest meaning, and the only option matching 'forced out/dismissed' sense is A. (Likely the stem word differs; A is the synonym among given choices.)

appearances.sentence: He drank excessive amount of liquor.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Excessive = inordinate (immoderate, beyond proper limits). 'Unreasonable' is weaker and not standard for quantity; 'inordinate' is the precise synonym.

appearances.sentence: The young are easily excitable when presented with strong emotional triggers.
appearances.solution: 'Excitable' means easily stirred up emotionally; its antonym is 'composed' (calm and collected). Matches option A: composed.

appearances.sentence: The church decided to excommunicate him for his actions.
appearances.solution: 'Excommunicate' means to officially exclude from membership of a church; the nearest synonym is 'expel'. Matches option C: expel.

appearances.sentence: The experience of Covid Pandemic was excruciating for much of the population.
appearances.solution: 'Excruciating' means intensely painful or agonizing; its antonym is 'mild' (gentle, not severe). Matches option D: mild.

appearances.sentence: I plan and execute.
appearances.solution: The synonym of 'execute' (to carry out a plan) is 'accomplish' (to achieve/complete). Matches option C: accomplish.

appearances.sentence: The soldier showed an exemplary courage.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. "Exemplary" means serving as a desirable model / ideal worthy of imitation; nearest synonym is "ideal". "Flawed" and "faulty" are opposite.

appearances.sentence: One's actions exemplify one's attitude and values.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Exemplify' means to illustrate/show by example; 'demonstrate' is nearest in meaning.

appearances.sentence: At the end of the marathon everybody was exhausted.
appearances.solution: 'Exhausted' means drained of energy; tired out. Matches option D: tired.

appearances.sentence: He was EXHILARATED to the outcome of the election results.
appearances.solution: Exhilarated means made intensely happy and lively, which is a far stronger feeling than simple approval, so 'overjoyed' is the match. 'Satisfied' is the trap because it is positive but much milder. 'Surprised' and 'disappointed' describe different reactions altogether. Matches option D.

appearances.sentence: Winning the World Cup was the most exhilarating moment for the Indian cricket team.
