appearances.sentence: Choose the word which is most OPPOSITE in meaning to the word given: RATIFICATION
appearances.solution: Ratification is formal approval or confirmation, so 'disapproval' is its opposite and the only option that is both a noun and semantically opposed. 'Disagreeable' and 'disturbing' are adjectives, and 'denial' opposes assertion rather than approval. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: RAVINE
appearances.solution: Ravine names a deep, narrow cleft in the ground, and abyss names the same idea of a yawning chasm. The remaining three - lucid, patent and palpable - all mean clear or obvious and belong to an entirely different sense. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: His hand-writing is readable.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Antonym of 'readable/legible' is 'illegible' (unable to be read). Well-written, decipherable and comprehensible are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: She rebuffed all suggestions from her friends.
appearances.solution: The concept is synonym identification: 'rebuffed' means rejected/snubbed. 'Rejected' is the nearest synonym. Matches option B: rejected.

appearances.sentence: Her rebuttal that she was not involved in the case was considered by the court.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Rebuttal' means a refutation/denial of an argument. Its antonym is 'Acceptance'. (Refusal and Denial are synonyms.)

appearances.sentence: Friendship is always reciprocal.
appearances.solution: The key concept is antonym identification. 'Reciprocal' means mutual or shared; its antonym is 'one-sided'. Matches option B: one-sided.

appearances.sentence: The committee should recommend his name to the government.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. To recommend a name is to put it forward / suggest it favourably; the nearest synonym is "suggest". "Advise"/"counsel" mean to give advice, not to propose a name.

appearances.sentence: She undertook a reconnaissance of the entire issue.
appearances.solution: Reconnaissance means a survey or investigation of an area; 'investigation' is the nearest synonym. Matches option C: investigation.

appearances.sentence: I must have a chance to RECTIFY my error.
appearances.solution: “Rectify” means to correct or fix an error. Its opposite, “worsen,” means to make the situation or error even worse.

appearances.sentence: The redemption will now depend on his new strategy of inclusiveness.
appearances.solution: 'Redemption' means the action of saving or being saved from sin, error, or evil; also means retrieval or recovery. 'Retrieval' is the closest option. Matches option A: retrieval.

appearances.sentence: Krishna is a redoubtable person.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Redoubtable' = formidable, commanding respect/fear. The opposite is 'unimpressive'. 'Formidable', 'fearsome', 'awe inspiring' are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: A trip to the hills was refreshing.
appearances.solution: 'Refreshing' means invigorating or revitalizing; the antonym is 'wearying' (tiring, exhausting). Matches option B: wearying.

appearances.sentence: The RELUCTANCE of the officer was obvious.
appearances.solution: “RELUCTANCE” means unwillingness or hesitation to do something. The opposite of this is “eagerness,” which indicates a strong willingness or enthusiasm to act. The other options—”hesitation,” “enjoyment,” and “unwillingness”—either align with or are unrelated to the meaning of “reluctance.”

appearances.sentence: Doctors are reluctant to take rural postings despite big salary offers.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Reluctant' (unwilling) is nearest to 'disinclined'. Eager and fervent are opposites; unrepentant is unrelated.

appearances.sentence: He was a reluctant learner.
appearances.solution: 'Reluctant' means unwilling or hesitant. Its synonym is 'unwilling'. Matches option C: unwilling.

appearances.sentence: RELUCTANTLY
appearances.solution: Reluctantly means unwillingly; the opposite is willingly. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: The decision of the Union Government to repeal the Urban Land Ceiling Act has been welcomed by all.
appearances.solution: 'Repeal' means to revoke or cancel a law officially. Matches option C: cancel.

appearances.sentence: My daughter is my replica.
appearances.solution: Replica means an exact copy or duplicate; 'clone' is the nearest synonym. Matches option B: clone.

appearances.sentence: The officer was reprimanded by the court for delaying the case.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Reprimanded' means to be rebuked/scolded formally; 'admonished' is nearest in meaning.

appearances.sentence: The authorities have reprimanded the subordinate officer for violating the protocol.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Reprimanded' (rebuked) is nearest to 'admonished'. Extolled is the opposite (praised); purported and 'required an apology' do not match.

appearances.sentence: His conduct brought him reproach from all quarters.
appearances.solution: The correct answer is (a) rebuke. The term “reproach” refers to an expression of disapproval or criticism. “Rebuke” is a synonym that also means a sharp criticism or reprimand. The other options (sympathy, indifference, remorse) do not align with the meaning of “reproach.”

appearances.sentence: The soldiers repulsed the enemy.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. To repulse an enemy is to drive them back / beat off an attack; the nearest synonym is "repelled" (to repel an attack = to repulse). "Defeated" is broader; repulse specifically means to drive back.

appearances.sentence: Macbeth is a morally repulsive character.
appearances.solution: The word 'repulsive' means causing disgust or aversion; its antonym is 'attractive' — pleasing or appealing. Matches option B: attractive.

appearances.sentence: The earthquake destroyed thousands of people’s lives but I was struck by the incredible resilience of the survivors I met.
appearances.solution: Resilience is the capacity to absorb a shock and recover from it. Potency and tenacity are strengths of the same family, and obstinate is not even a noun and so cannot replace it. Weakness is the plain reverse of that capacity to withstand and bounce back. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: The actor narrated the story in a resonant voice.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Resonant' means deep, clear and continuing to sound; rich and full. The nearest synonym is 'deep'. 'Soft', 'harsh' and 'quivering' do not capture the rich, sonorous quality.

appearances.sentence: Mohan is quite reticent.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Reticent (reserved, untalkative) is opposite to garrulous (talkative). Taciturn/reserved/quiet are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: He appears to be reticent.
appearances.solution: 'Reticent' means not revealing one's thoughts; reserved. Its synonym is 'withdrawn'. Matches option D: withdrawn.

appearances.sentence: His deeds had retrograde results.
appearances.solution: 'Retrograde' means directed backwards or declining; its antonym is 'progressive' (moving forward, improving). Matches option A: progressive.

appearances.sentence: He used to be known among his colleagues for his righteousness.
appearances.solution: 'Righteousness' means moral virtue; its antonym is 'iniquity' (wickedness/injustice). Matches option A: iniquity.

appearances.sentence: A truly respectable old man is a ripe person.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. "Ripe" applied to a person who is old/respectable means fully developed in judgement and experience, i.e. mature. "Seasoned" is close but implies practised by experience; "mature" is the nearest single-word synonym for ripe (ripe = fully matured).

appearances.sentence: Choose the word which is most OPPOSITE in meaning to the word given: ROUGH
appearances.solution: In its primary sense rough describes an uneven surface, whose direct opposite is smooth. 'Refined' and 'polite' oppose only the secondary sense of coarse manners. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: She had a ruddy, open face and an oddly guileless manner.
appearances.solution: 'Ruddy' means having a healthy red complexion; its antonym is 'cadaverous' (pale, like a corpse). Matches option B: cadaverous.

appearances.sentence: Early humans may have had a rudimentary understanding of certain mathematical concepts.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Rudimentary means basic, undeveloped — nearest in meaning to elementary.

appearances.sentence: My mother has been working hard for the last two weeks and she feels run down.
appearances.solution: 'Run down' means exhausted/in poor health. Its antonym is energetic. Matches option B: energetic.

appearances.sentence: This process taught me the importance of being a ruthless editor. I learnt that if a piece of information can be deleted without impacting the narrative flow, then it didn't belong there.
appearances.solution: Ruthless means showing no pity, which is why the sentence uses it of an editor who deletes without hesitation. Callous, meaning hardened and unfeeling, is its close synonym and is the trap set here. Boorish means rude and ill-mannered and acrimonious means bitter in tone, and neither of those reverses pitilessness. Compassionate, full of pity for others, does. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: SACRILEGE
appearances.solution: The term sacrilege refers to the violation or profanation of something that is held sacred, such as a religious belief, place or object, whereas blasphemy also refers to the act of showing disrespect or lack of reverence for something sacred, particularly religious things. Therefore, “blasphemy” is the word most similar in meaning to “sacrilege”.

appearances.sentence: Akbar the great was a sagacious ruler.
appearances.solution: The correct answer is (d) unwise, as it is the opposite of “sagacious,” which means wise or showing good judgment. The other options (haughty, cunning, rude) do not directly contrast with “sagacious.”

appearances.sentence: He was known for his sagacity.
appearances.solution: 'Sagacity' means having good judgment or wisdom. Its antonym is 'ignorance'. Matches option C: ignorance.

appearances.sentence: His salubrious words calmed the students.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Salubrious means health-giving / wholesome / beneficial; among the options, 'pleasant' is nearest in meaning and fits 'calmed the students'.

appearances.sentence: Ravi is jovial and he makes the environment sanguine.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Sanguine' means optimistic/cheerful. Its antonym is 'Pessimistic'.

appearances.sentence: The sardonic nature of her stories made her stand out among the contemporary writers.
appearances.solution: Sardonic means grimly mocking or cynical; 'mocking' is the nearest synonym. Matches option C: mocking.

appearances.sentence: She wore a sardonic smile on her face.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Sardonic' = grimly mocking, scornful. 'Mocking' is the exact synonym. 'Respectful', 'reverential', 'deferential' are opposites.

appearances.sentence: His sartorial manner is judged.
appearances.solution: 'Sartorial' relates to tailoring and stylish dress; its antonym in context is 'unstylish'. Matches option A: unstylish.

appearances.sentence: Can medicines save us from death?
appearances.solution: Answer: C. "Save us from death" means to keep us safe from / preserve us against death; the nearest synonym is "protect" (protect us from death). "Rescue" implies extracting from an existing danger after the fact; "protect" best fits guarding against death.

appearances.sentence: She was upset seeing the SCATTERED documents.
appearances.solution: “Scattered” means spread out or dispersed, so the opposite would be “gathered,” which means brought together or collected in one place. The other options, “perished,” “dissipated,” and “sprinkled,” do not convey the opposite meaning of “scattered.”

appearances.sentence: The public was sceptical about the new government policy.
appearances.solution: The concept is synonym identification: 'sceptical' means doubtful/questioning. 'Doubtful' is the nearest synonym. Matches option C: doubtful.

appearances.sentence: It has been to start a scurrilous attack on all his opponents.
appearances.solution: 'Scurrilous' means grossly abusive or defamatory; its opposite is respectful praise — admiration ('scandalous' is a synonym). Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: Ravi loves seclusion. Therefore, he lives in the mountains.
appearances.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Seclusion' means the state of being private and away from others; 'solitariness' is the closest match. Matches option D: solitariness.

appearances.sentence: A sedentary lifestyle could increase your levels of exhaustion.
appearances.solution: Sedentary describes a life spent sitting still and taking little exercise. Dormant, apathetic and somnambulant all keep to that same idea of inactivity or sluggishness. Animated means lively and full of movement, which reverses it. Matches option D.

appearances.sentence: For the aspiring East India Company that looked at every opportunity for expansion and self-aggrandisement, the century had to be projected as one of instability.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Self-aggrandisement' means promoting one's own power/importance/wealth. The opposite is 'humility' (modesty, lowliness). 'Upliftment' and 'elevation' suggest raising up; 'exaggeration' is unrelated to the self-promotion sense.

appearances.sentence: The Earth's climate sensitivity is conventionally defined as the equilibrium temperature increase caused by a doubling of carbon dioxide.
appearances.solution: The antonym of 'sensitivity' (receptiveness/responsiveness to stimuli) is 'imperviousness' (inability to be affected). Matches option A: imperviousness.

appearances.sentence: The serene beauty of Kashmir had a soothing effect on his mind.
appearances.solution: The word 'serene' means calm and peaceful; its antonym is 'turbulent' — characterized by conflict or confusion. Matches option D: turbulent.

appearances.sentence: He is very serious by temperament.
appearances.solution: Serious means solemn or earnest; the antonym in temperament context is trivial (not taking things seriously / frivolous). Matches option B: trivial.

appearances.sentence: They served fruits after the dinner.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. To serve food/fruits is to present or offer it to others; "offered" is the nearest synonym in this context. "Waited" (as in wait on) is less direct than offered.

appearances.sentence: Henry is so SERVILE that other people take advantage of him.
appearances.solution: “Servile” refers to having an excessive willingness to serve or please others, often to the point of being submissive. The opposite of this is “arrogant,” which means having an exaggerated sense of one’s importance or superiority. The other options do not directly oppose the meaning of “servile.”

appearances.sentence: It is unwise to sever diplomatic relations with a neighbouring country over small matters.
appearances.solution: 'Sever' means to cut or break off; 'cut off' is the closest synonym. 'Estrange' means to cause to feel alienated (related but not equivalent), 'engage' is an antonym. Matches option C: cut off.

appearances.sentence: His family severed ties with him for marrying inter- caste.
appearances.solution: The word "severed" means to break or cut off, in terms of relationships or connections. The opposite of "severed" in this context would be "joined," which means to come together or form a connection.

appearances.sentence: His behaviour shocked me.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Shocked = appalled. Pacified is opposite; entreated/scintillated unrelated.

appearances.sentence: Rakesh delivered a slanderous speech.
appearances.solution: The word 'slanderous' means making false spoken statements that damage a person's reputation; 'abusive' is the closest synonym indicating harmful speech. Matches option A: abusive.

appearances.sentence: He gave a slapdash performance.
appearances.solution: 'Slapdash' means done hastily and carelessly; its opposite is careful ('hasty' and 'haphazard' are synonyms). Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: He drove his car through slimy road to reach your office.
appearances.solution: The word "slimy" describes something that is slippery, dirty, or covered in a thick and unpleasant substance. The opposite of "slimy" in this context would be "clean," meaning free from dirt or mess.

appearances.sentence: Heavy outfits make the movement of trekkers SLUGGISH.
appearances.solution: The word “sluggish” means slow- moving or lacking energy. Its opposite is “active,” which refers to being energetic, quick, or lively. This makes “active” the most appropriate antonym in this context.

appearances.sentence: The newly made road was smooth.
appearances.solution: 'Smooth' means even and flat; its antonym is 'rutted' (having ruts, uneven). Options B and C do not directly mean rough/uneven as a surface. Matches option A: rutted.

appearances.sentence: They smothered the fire in the building.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. To smother a fire is to extinguish/douse it by cutting off air.

appearances.sentence: The baby could not move as the place was soggy.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Soggy' means saturated/wet. Its antonym is 'Dry'. (Sodden and Wet are synonyms.)

appearances.sentence: At last she was able to get some solace as the matter has been resolved amicably.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Solace' means comfort or consolation in distress. Its opposite is 'aggravation' (worsening of distress). 'comfort' and 'relief' are synonyms; 'punishment' is unrelated. 'aggravation'.

appearances.sentence: His solemnity is celebrated.
appearances.solution: 'Solemnity' means the quality of being formal, dignified, and serious; 'dignity' is the nearest synonym. Matches option D: dignity.

appearances.sentence: The song had a SOPORIFIC effect on the child.
appearances.solution: “SOPORIFIC” refers to something that causes or induces sleep. In this context, it means the song made the child feel sleepy. The other options like “soothing,” “terrific,” and “supreme” do not specifically convey the idea of inducing sleep.

appearances.sentence: SPLAY
appearances.solution: To splay is to spread out wide, as in splayed fingers or splayed legs, so spread is the match. Defile means to pollute, jade means to wear out or dull, and fray means to unravel at the edges. Matches option D.

appearances.sentence: Too many cooks spoil the broth.
appearances.solution: 'Spoil' means to damage or ruin; its antonym is 'embellish' (to enhance or beautify). Matches option C: embellish.

appearances.sentence: The poet said that poetry is a spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Spontaneous' means unplanned, arising naturally without forethought. Its opposite is 'deliberate' (intentional, planned). 'prepared' and 'well executed' are weaker; 'alerted' is unrelated. 'deliberate'.

appearances.sentence: Everywhere they go, they squander their earnings.
appearances.solution: The concept is antonym identification: 'squander' means to waste carelessly. 'Manage' implies careful handling, the antonym. Options A, B are synonyms; C is unrelated. Matches option D: manage.

appearances.sentence: SQUANDER
appearances.solution: The most appropriate synonym for “squander” is (b) Frivol. “Squander” means to waste something, especially money or resources, recklessly or foolishly, which is similar to “frivol,” meaning to behave in a carefree or reckless way.

appearances.sentence: It is terrible for people to die of starvation.
appearances.solution: The word 'starvation' means suffering or dying from lack of food; 'hunger' is the closest synonym. Matches option D: hunger.

appearances.sentence: The statutory corporate tax which forms the major income of the government has not changed this year.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. Statutory = fixed/required by statute, i.e. by law; lawful. Nearest synonym among the options is legal.

appearances.sentence: Mohan is his steadfast friend.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. Antonym of 'steadfast' (loyal, firm) is 'unreliable'. Committed, unwavering and unfaltering are synonyms of steadfast.

appearances.sentence: The captain produced yet another stellar show to make her team enter the semi-finals.
appearances.solution: The item asks for the word nearest in meaning to the underlined one. Something described as stellar is outstanding, so 'extraordinary' is the match. 'Poor' and 'not a great' are opposites, and 'eclipse' plays on the astronomical family the word belongs to without carrying its sense of excellence. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: The captain produced yet another stellar show to make her team enter the semi-finals.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Stellar' means outstanding or exceptionally good; 'extraordinary' is nearest.

appearances.sentence: The debate was highly stimulating.
appearances.solution: The key concept is antonym identification. 'Stimulating' means interesting and exciting; its antonym is 'boring'. Matches option C: boring.

appearances.sentence: STINGY
appearances.solution: The term stingy refers to one who is unwilling to spend money or be generous, similar in meaning to miserly, which describes someone who hoards money and is unwilling to share or spend it. The other options—violent, cautious and quarrelsome—are unrelated to the meaning of stingy.

appearances.sentence: STINGY
appearances.solution: The most appropriate synonym for “stingy” is (b) Miser. “Stingy” means being unwilling to spend or give, similar to “miser,” which refers to a person who hoards money and is very reluctant to spend it.

appearances.sentence: The jewels have been stolen from her bedroom.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. "Stolen" = taken dishonestly; "embezzled" (to steal/misappropriate, especially money or valuables in one's trust) is the nearest in meaning. The other options are unrelated.

appearances.sentence: After the sudden demise of the director of the company, the employees felt stranded.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Stranded means left helpless without support — closest to marooned (left isolated/abandoned).

appearances.sentence: My friend is as stubborn as a mule.
appearances.solution: 'Stubborn' means refusing to change; 'obstinate' is its closest synonym. Matches option C: obstinate.

appearances.sentence: With little access to medical care, many of them succumbed to exhaustion, starvation and disease.
appearances.solution: To succumb to something is to stop resisting it and give way to it, so those who succumbed to exhaustion, starvation and disease were overcome by them and gave in. Capitulate carries exactly that sense of ceasing to resist and yielding to a force one can no longer withstand. Of the others, to battle is the opposite, since it means to go on resisting; defeated will not fit either the sense or the grammar, because a person is defeated by a hardship and never defeated to it, whereas the sentence has succumbed to; and sonorous, meaning deep and resonant in sound, has nothing to do with the meaning at all. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: It's the only treatment suitable for cancer.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. "Suitable" means appropriate/fitting; its opposite is "impertinent" in the sense of inappropriate/not pertinent. "Befitting" and "congenial" are synonyms; "insufficient" relates to quantity, not suitability.

appearances.sentence: SULKY
appearances.solution: The most appropriate synonym for “sulky” is (d) Dismal. “Sulky” refers to a mood of being silently upset or in a bad temper, often displaying gloom or unhappiness, which is similar to “dismal,” meaning depressing or gloomy.

appearances.sentence: I do not want you to lead a life of sycophancy as you did during the foreign rule.
appearances.solution: Sycophancy means excessive flattery or servile compliance to gain favour. The nearest meaning is flattery. Matches option D: flattery.

appearances.sentence: He gave his TACIT approval to the proposition.
appearances.solution: Tacit approval is approval understood without being stated aloud, so 'implied' is the word that matches. 'Loud' is its direct opposite in this respect. 'Full' and 'clean' describe how complete or unconditional the approval was, not whether it was ever put into words. Matches option D.

appearances.sentence: Do not indulge in tautology.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Tautology' (needless repetition / redundancy of wording) is nearest to 'prolixity' (verbosity, wordiness). Truth telling/foretelling/telepathic do not match.

appearances.sentence: She had the TEMERITY to call her teacher a liar.
appearances.solution: The term “Temerity” means excessive boldness or audacity, often in a way that is disrespectful or arrogant. “Impudence” is a synonym that also refers to shameless boldness or disrespect. Therefore, impudence is the most fitting word in this context.

appearances.sentence: Tempestuous behaviour would not yield much in any place.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Tempestuous' means turbulent, stormy or violent; its opposite is 'relaxed' (calm). Passionate/intense/windy align with it.

appearances.sentence: Radha often goes tempestuous while debating.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Antonym of 'tempestuous' (stormy, turbulent) is 'calm'. Violent, fierce and vehement are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: Ramesh has a tempestuous relationship with his neighbours.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Tempestuous' means stormy/turbulent; its opposite is 'tranquil' (calm), while tumultuous and riotous are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: Tempestuous behaviour would not yield much in any place.
appearances.solution: 'Tempestuous' means stormy and violent, so its opposite is a word for calm: 'relaxed'. The other three all lean the same way as the underlined word - 'passionate' and 'intense' are near-synonyms of its figurative sense, and 'windy' echoes the literal storm it is built on. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: There is a tendency to treat social changes as mere development in terms of accumulation of wealth.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Tendency = an inclination/predisposition to act or think in a particular way. Nearest synonym is predisposition.

appearances.sentence: He is suffering from a terminal disease.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. A 'terminal' disease is one that ends in death and cannot be cured — nearest to 'incurable'. Chronic means long-lasting (not necessarily fatal); incurable best captures 'terminal'.

appearances.sentence: Rahul is always thrifty.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Thrifty means careful with money / frugal, which is nearest to 'economical'. 'Extravagant' and 'reckless' are opposites.

appearances.sentence: Thrifty as he is, he can well afford to live within his means
appearances.solution: The correct answer is (d) extravagant, as it is the opposite of “thrifty,” meaning spending excessively or wastefully. The other options (careless, instinctive, sentimental) are unrelated to the meaning of “thrifty.”

appearances.sentence: This boy is very timid.
appearances.solution: 'Timid' means lacking confidence or shy; 'shy' is the nearest synonym. 'Courageous' is the antonym. Matches option B: shy.

appearances.sentence: She tormented me with her detached behaviour.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. Tormented means to cause distress/suffering; distressed is nearest in meaning.

appearances.sentence: The magazine article provided ideas for activities designed to shake off the torpor of a rainy day.
appearances.solution: Torpor is a noun meaning sluggishness and want of energy. Naive, dispassionate and fervent are all adjectives and cannot replace a noun in the sentence, and fervent, meaning passionate, would in any case reverse the sense. Tepidity is the noun for lukewarmness and lack of enthusiasm, which is the flatness a rainy day produces. Matches option C.

appearances.sentence: Choose the word nearest in meaning to: TRAMP
appearances.solution: A 'tramp' is a vagrant who roams from place to place, i.e. a 'wanderer'. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: Peace and tranquility are instruments which would boost the development of society.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. Tranquillity = calmness, quiet, peace. Antonym is uproar. (Calm and serenity are synonyms.)

appearances.sentence: Life is transient in nature.
appearances.solution: The word 'transient' means lasting for only a short time; its antonym is 'eternal' — lasting forever. Matches option C: eternal.

appearances.sentence: No one knew what transpired during the meeting.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. To 'transpire' means to happen / to come to be known (emerge). The nearest synonym among the options is 'emerged'. 'Merged' is a sound-alike distractor; 'exchanged'/'was spoken' are narrower.

appearances.sentence: The poorly conducted workshop was a travesty of the initial vision document.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. A travesty is a distorted, debased imitation — a mockery of the original.

appearances.sentence: It was due to TREACHEROUS leaders that he decided to leave the party.
appearances.solution: “Treacherous” refers to being deceitful, dishonest, or disloyal. “Disloyal” fits as the most appropriate synonym, meaning not loyal or faithless, which aligns with the idea of treacherous behaviour.

appearances.sentence: TRIVIAL issues have never bothered me.
appearances.solution: “Trivial” refers to something of little importance or value. Its opposite is “significant,” which means something important or meaningful. The other options do not convey the opposite meaning of “trivial.”

appearances.sentence: His truancy is detrimental.
appearances.solution: 'Truancy' means the practice of staying away from school or duty without permission; 'absenteeism' is the nearest synonym. Matches option D: absenteeism.

appearances.sentence: All of us are living in turbulent times.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. Turbulent means disturbed and unsettled. Its opposite is tranquil (calm); capricious, desolate and obstreperous are not opposites.

appearances.sentence: We were living in turbulent times.
appearances.solution: 'Turbulent' means characterized by conflict, disorder, or confusion; its antonym is 'calm' (peaceful and settled). Matches option C: calm.

appearances.sentence: To say that the pandemic is done and dusted with would be an understatement.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. An understatement is a statement that represents something as smaller or less important than it is — i.e. underplaying significance.

appearances.sentence: Most of the decisions taken by the officer were unjust.
appearances.solution: 'Unjust' means not based on or behaving according to what is right. Its antonym is correct/fair. Matches option C: correct.

appearances.sentence: Do not indulge in unmindful activities, please.
appearances.solution: The word 'unmindful' means not conscious or aware; its antonym is 'vigilant' — carefully observant and attentive. Matches option A: vigilant.

appearances.sentence: Unrest in some pockets made the city dwellers confine themselves at home.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. Unrest = disturbance/turbulence/unease. Antonym is Calm. (Turbulence, unease, apprehension are synonyms.)

appearances.sentence: This ushered in a large-scale social, economic, and political transformation.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. To 'usher in' means to introduce, bring in, lead in. The opposite is 'obstructed' (blocked, prevented). 'Led', 'conducted', 'directed' are near-synonyms.

appearances.sentence: The HR Manager was able to utilize the specific skills of each member of the team assembled for the project.
appearances.solution: 'Utilize' means to make practical use of; 'harness' captures the same meaning of channeling skills effectively. Matches option A: harness.

appearances.sentence: His views on the matter are utopian.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Utopian' means idealistic, impossibly perfect. The nearest synonym is 'ideal'. 'Realistic'/'practicable' are antonyms; 'materialistic' is unrelated.

appearances.sentence: Sohan is a vain person.
appearances.solution: The word 'vain' means having excessive pride in one's appearance or achievements; its antonym is 'modest' — humble and unassuming. Matches option A: modest.

appearances.sentence: VALIDATE
appearances.solution: The most appropriate synonym for “validate” is (c) Corroborate. “Validate” means to confirm or make something valid, which is similar to “corroborate,” meaning to support or confirm something with evidence.

appearances.sentence: The various facets of life can be found reflected in a large city.
appearances.solution: The word 'various' means of different kinds, or several; 'several' is the closest synonym. Matches option A: several.

appearances.sentence: He had been vehement in opposing the idea.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Vehement means forceful and passionate. Its opposite is subdued (restrained, quiet); ardent, fervent and impassioned are synonyms.

appearances.sentence: The bill received a vehement resistance from the opposition party in the Parliament.
appearances.solution: The key concept is antonym identification. 'Vehement' means intense or forceful; its antonym is 'apathetic' (showing no interest or enthusiasm). Matches option B: apathetic.

appearances.sentence: Our teacher told us not to be verbose while writing.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Verbose' means using or expressing in more words than are needed; long-winded, wordy. The nearest in meaning is 'exaggerate' (overdo/overstate). 'Short' and 'succinct' are antonyms; 'informal' is unrelated. Note: 'verbose' is an adjective while options mix forms, but 'exaggerate' best captures the excess/overuse sense.

appearances.sentence: He became VERBOSE after a few drinks.
appearances.solution: The term “Verbose” refers to someone who uses more words than necessary, often speaking at length. This matches the meaning of “talkative,” which describes a person who talks a lot. The other options are not synonyms: “aggressive” refers to being forceful or hostile, “decisive” refers to being clear and firm in decision-making, and “exhaustive” means thorough, which is unrelated to the idea of talking.

appearances.sentence: Sheela appeared to be vexed.
appearances.solution: 'Vexed' means annoyed or worried; the nearest synonym is 'displeased'. Matches option C: displeased.

appearances.sentence: In this competition, he has become the VICTOR.
appearances.solution: “VICTOR” refers to someone who has won or emerged victorious. The opposite of this is “vanquished,” which means someone who has been defeated in a competition or conflict. The other options, such as “beaten,” “frustrated,” and “disappointed,” do not precisely convey the direct opposite of “victor” as clearly as “vanquished.”

appearances.sentence: The question is not whether the court vindicates him with regard to his involvement in the case, but how he feels about it.
appearances.solution: Answer: C. 'Vindicate' means to clear of blame/acquit; the opposite is 'indicts' (to formally charge with a crime).

appearances.sentence: People fear him because of his VINDICTIVE nature.
appearances.solution: “VINDICTIVE” refers to someone who has a strong desire for revenge or retribution, especially after being wronged. It describes a person who is motivated by a desire to get back at others. The other options like “violent,” “cruel,” and “irritable,” do not capture the focus on seeking revenge that “vindictive” implies.

appearances.sentence: The President condemned the act of violence during the celebration of the festival.
appearances.solution: 'Violence' means behavior involving force intended to hurt. Its antonym is restraint (controlled behaviour). Matches option C: restraint.

appearances.sentence: The vista of the villages is beautiful.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. A vista is a view or expansive scene — a landscape.

appearances.sentence: The thief had very vital information to pass on to the police.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Antonym of 'vital' (essential) is 'inessential'. Crucial, indispensable and fundamental are synonyms of vital.

appearances.sentence: His language is political and vitriolic.
appearances.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Vitriolic' means filled with bitter criticism; 'abusive' is the closest synonym. Matches option D: abusive.

appearances.sentence: The imagery used in the poem is vivid.
appearances.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Vivid' means producing powerful feelings or clear images; 'lively' is the closest synonym. Matches option A: lively.

appearances.sentence: His descriptions are VIVID.
appearances.solution: “VIVID” refers to something that is described in a way that is clear, full of details, and easy to imagine, often with strong imagery. So, “detailed” is the most appropriate meaning in this context. The other options do not capture the essence of vivid descriptions.

appearances.sentence: Not everyone finds a vocation which suits one's aptitude.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. 'Vocation' means a calling, profession or occupation; 'occupation' is nearest.

appearances.sentence: Not everyone finds a vocation which suits one's aptitude.
appearances.solution: The underlined word means the trade or calling a person is suited to and takes up as their life's work, so 'occupation' is nearest in meaning. 'Liking' captures the enjoyment but not the work; 'attitude' is only a near-homophone of 'aptitude', which the sentence already uses separately; 'approach' names a manner of doing something, not a calling. Matches option D.

appearances.sentence: Reading details about suicide cases can push vulnerable people taking the extreme step.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Vulnerable' means exposed/susceptible to harm. Its antonym is 'Impervious' (not affected, resistant). 'Helpless' and 'Defenseless' are synonyms; 'Imperious' is unrelated (domineering).

appearances.sentence: A human being is always vulnerable to other human beings.
appearances.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Vulnerable' means susceptible to harm; 'defenceless' is the closest synonym. Matches option C: defenceless.

appearances.sentence: Rakesh is vulnerable to political pressure.
appearances.solution: Answer: D. "Vulnerable" means open to harm/easily affected; its opposite is "resilient" (able to withstand or recover, not easily affected). "Weak", "unguarded" and "exposed" are synonyms of vulnerable.

appearances.sentence: People argue about why Venus is so much warmer than the Earth.
appearances.solution: The antonym of 'warmer' (higher temperature) is 'colder' (lower temperature). Matches option B: colder.

appearances.sentence: WHOLESOME
appearances.solution: “Wholesome” refers to something that is good for health or beneficial in a moral or physical sense. The opposite of wholesome would be “unhealthy”, which refers to something harmful or not good for health.

appearances.sentence: Malaria is a widespread disease.
appearances.solution: The key concept is antonym identification. 'Widespread' means found over a large area; its antonym is 'rare'. Matches option D: rare.

appearances.sentence: He listened to me with equanimity.
appearances.solution: 'Equanimity' means mental calmness and composure; its synonym in manner is 'patiently'. Matches option C: patiently.

appearances.sentence: There prevailed a woebegone feeling in the room.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. 'Woebegone' means sorrowful/sad. Its antonym is 'Cheerful'.

appearances.sentence: Wooing everyone over an issue for support will not serve much purpose.
appearances.solution: Answer: A. 'Wooing' means seeking to win over or persuade; its opposite is 'discouraging'. Encouraging/pursuing/persuading are close in meaning.

appearances.sentence: Wooing everyone over an issue for support will not serve much purpose.
appearances.solution: To woo is to court someone's favour and coax them round to your side, so the opposite is to put them off: 'discouraging'. The other three all describe the same winning-over that the underlined word does - 'encouraging', 'pursuing' and 'persuading' are on its side, not against it. Matches option A.

appearances.sentence: His lectures are often wordy and pointless.
appearances.solution: Answer: B. Antonym of 'wordy' (using too many words) is 'concise' (brief). Diffuse, garrulous and voluble are synonyms of wordy.

appearances.sentence: The discussion was wound up after a long and fruitful exchange of views.
appearances.solution: The phrase 'wound up' means brought to a conclusion/ended. The discussion was concluded after the exchange. Matches option D: concluded.

appearances.sentence: WRY
appearances.solution: Wry describes a face or manner twisted by displeasure, as in pulling a wry face at bad news, so vexed is the closest match. Jubilant sits at the opposite end of the same scale, which is what makes it the trap; resolved and wolfish are unrelated. Matches option B.

appearances.sentence: He has been yearning to go home.
appearances.solution: The synonym of 'yearning' (longing intensely for something) is 'hankering' (craving). Matches option D: hankering.
